name: Crypto and investing
intro: Where the wallet and exchange are honest and reliable, and where funds suddenly end up frozen.

apps.title: MetaTrader 5
apps.verdict: MetaTrader 5 remains the industry standard for professional trading: it connects to hundreds of brokers and supports scripts and expert advisors. The mobile version falls short of desktop when it comes to placing stop-losses and take-profits, especially on a tablet.
apps.loved: Compatibility with any broker and a complete technical-analysis toolkit all in one app.
apps.weak: Setting a stop-loss and take-profit on a mobile screen is awkward: the lines appear outside the visible area.
apps.whoFor: A professional trader working through a broker with an MT5 connector.

apps.title: Solflare: Solana Crypto Wallet
apps.verdict: Solflare is rightly considered the reference non-custodial wallet for the Solana ecosystem: staking, DeFi, and swaps are implemented natively and run reliably. Occasional regressions after updates and a disappearing transaction tab spoil the picture.
apps.loved: Native SOL staking and interaction with DeFi protocols directly from the wallet, no redirects needed.
apps.weak: Updates sometimes remove key screens, like transaction history, for several versions in a row.
apps.whoFor: Active participants in the Solana ecosystem, from staking to DeFi.

apps.title: River: Buy Bitcoin
apps.verdict: River handles the core job well: buy bitcoin, set up recurring purchases, and stop worrying about custody. The serious flaw is opaque account closures with no explanation, which erodes trust in the platform.
apps.loved: Built-in DCA with a flexible schedule and proof of reserves make accumulating bitcoin nearly automatic.
apps.weak: Accounts are closed without warning or explanation, sometimes right after a deposit.
apps.whoFor: Americans who want to methodically stack bitcoin without extra coins or complexity.

apps.title: Tangem - Crypto wallet
apps.verdict: The best hardware wallet in the category for the balance of simplicity and security: an NFC card instead of a device and a straightforward onboarding flow. Key gaps: no purchase average price display, transaction history not working for all assets, and some promised networks waiting for support for months.
apps.loved: An NFC card instead of a bulky device, plus full self-custody without a seed phrase in the cloud.
apps.weak: No display of average purchase price or total return per asset in the portfolio.
apps.whoFor: A crypto holder who puts storage security above trading convenience.

quotes.text: I like the set up and the simplicity of the app but I would love it if I was able to see my average cost per for my holdings!!
How is there not a average cost base on the app for currencies? I should be able too know my average cost for selling especially if I add from different exchanges.

I was staking about 5sol, i unstaked all my coins , but i didn't receive all of them , native staking bar has matter and don't show me the button to unstaking and it's processing yet to show the balance but not anything yet.

Continuous syncing issues requiring reinstall to fix. Made team aware of the, in their words, "known bug" to which reinstalling was the working "solution". Once again, a few updates later, I cannot access my assets requiring another round of reinstalling and setting up the app.

apps.title: Rainbow - Ethereum Wallet
apps.verdict: Rainbow stands out for exceptionally well-crafted mobile UX among Ethereum wallets, and its audience values that, but periodic browser crashes and unstable WalletConnect behavior limit its use as a full DeFi tool.
apps.loved: Interaction patterns are designed for touchscreens so carefully that using the wallet feels natural.
apps.weak: Custom RPC provider is unavailable in the mobile version even though the browser extension has it.
apps.whoFor: Active Ethereum ecosystem participants who care about design.

apps.title: tastytrade: Invest & Trade
apps.verdict: Tastytrade is rightly considered the best mobile platform for options trading in terms of execution quality and position analysis screen design. The main issues are post-update stability and stale watchlist quotes.
apps.loved: Depth of options analysis tools on mobile that competitors do not match.
apps.weak: After updates the platform periodically breaks: P/L resets to zero, quotes freeze, trade notifications duplicate.
apps.whoFor: Active options traders working from their phone.

apps.title: CoinGlass - Bitcoin & Crypto
apps.verdict: CoinGlass is the most informative tool for analyzing market positioning: liquidation maps, long/short data, and on-chain metrics in one place without ads. The mobile version falls short of desktop in functionality, and filters behave inconsistently.
apps.loved: Liquidation maps and the long/short ratio give real insight into market tension ahead of key levels.
apps.weak: Filters require an app restart, and liquidation maps on mobile cannot be scaled the same way as on desktop.
apps.whoFor: Active traders who analyze market structure before opening positions.

apps.title: DEX Screener
apps.verdict: DEX Screener is the best mobile tool for monitoring decentralized pairs: data depth, multi-chain coverage, and quote refresh speed are valued by memecoin traders. The main pain points are unreliable alerts and removed chart drawing tools.
apps.loved: Complete DEX pair data across dozens of networks in one place with fast search.
apps.weak: Alerts fire inconsistently or not at all, which is critical for scalpers.
apps.whoFor: Active traders in decentralized networks and hunters of new tokens.

apps.title: Kraken: Buy Crypto & Stocks
apps.verdict: A reliable exchange with a clear interface and a wide range of assets that has built loyal users over time. The main product-level complaint: transferring funds requires manual email back-and-forth instead of an automated flow.
apps.loved: Wide asset selection and a sense of reliability from long-term users who describe it as honest and straightforward.
apps.weak: Transferring an account to another broker requires manual email chains of 10 or more messages with no clear instructions.
apps.whoFor: An experienced trader for whom breadth of instruments and exchange reputation matter.

apps.title: Cake Wallet
apps.verdict: Cake Wallet fills the rare niche of privacy coins with a genuinely working Monero wallet and responsive support, but the UI is unstable between updates and some swaps hang with no way to exit.
apps.loved: Monero and privacy coin support at a level unavailable in most wallets.
apps.weak: The interface behaves unpredictably when switching between multiple wallets in a single session.
apps.whoFor: Users for whom transaction privacy matters more than convenience.

apps.title: Swan Bitcoin: Buy & Save
apps.verdict: Swan Bitcoin handles its single job well: scheduled bitcoin purchases on autopilot. But session authentication problems and opaque withdrawal timelines create anxiety when dealing with real amounts.
apps.loved: Simple automated bitcoin purchases on a schedule with no extra steps or distracting assets.
apps.weak: No display of unrealized profit or cost basis, so the user cannot see the real picture of their investment.
apps.whoFor: Long-term bitcoin accumulators who practice regular purchases.

apps.title: BingX: Buy Crypto & Stocks
apps.verdict: A convenient exchange for spot trading and futures with low fees and copy trading, but US users are blocked and the SMS code system for withdrawals periodically stops working.
apps.loved: Low fees, robust copy trading, and a user-friendly mobile interface for futures.
apps.weak: The TP order system has a 2000% PnL profit cap, which prevents holding a position through extreme moves.
apps.whoFor: Traders from CIS countries and Latin America looking for a Binance alternative.

apps.title: moomoo: Investing & Trading
apps.verdict: Good analytical tools for an active trader: solid charts, backtesting, and multi-instrument coverage. Restricting access to certain stocks undermines the platform's value for experienced users.
apps.loved: Everything in one screen: stocks, warrants, options, futures, plus live charts straight from a smartphone.
apps.weak: The platform started limiting available instruments and traders are moving to alternatives.
apps.whoFor: Beginner to intermediate traders who want a rich analytical interface.

apps.title: Ledger Wallet™ crypto app
apps.verdict: The best hardware wallet on the market for reliable asset protection with a solid mobile companion. The main issue of recent months: the mobile app has noticeably declined in stability, with more frequent crashes and freezes when connecting to the device.
apps.loved: The gold standard for cold crypto storage: private keys never leave the device.
apps.weak: The mobile app has become unstable after recent updates, with Bluetooth reconnecting on its own.
apps.whoFor: Long-term holders who store significant amounts and do not trade daily.

quotes.text: The Ledger has served me well in my crypto investments with excellent protection and I enjoy the simplicity of the app. The only thing I would like is an update on the app allowing users to see our average cost for each asset which is why I rated it 4 out of 5 stars.
Ledger is very handy and easy to navigate. If you are looking for a cold wallet, this is the go to.
Bluetooth has to re connect a lot and it's annoying
Terrible app. I can't update it from my phone, I need a PC. Constant unnecessary updates, without which it stops working.

apps.title: Zengo: Crypto & Bitcoin Wallet
apps.verdict: Zengo stands out for its no-seed-phrase model and is perceived as a reliable non-custodial wallet, but transaction send failures and weak support undermine trust exactly when it is needed most.
apps.loved: Biometric protection without a seed phrase gives a sense of security without technical complexity.
apps.weak: Transactions hang without a clear reason, and support responds with scripts and does not resolve real problems.
apps.whoFor: Crypto beginners for whom security matters without complicated setup.

apps.title: Pera Algo Wallet
apps.verdict: Pera is the best option for those working with Algorand: transactions are instant, network fees are negligible, and WalletConnect is built in. The main pain points are high swap fees inside the app and occasional errors during swaps.
apps.loved: Algorand network transactions settle in seconds at a fraction of a cent in fees.
apps.weak: Swapping tokens inside the app costs more than on external platforms.
apps.whoFor: ALGO holders and active participants in the Algorand ecosystem.

apps.title: Bitget Wallet: Crypto, Markets
apps.verdict: Bitget Wallet handles the core job of non-custodial storage and works with a large number of networks. The GetGas feature helps new users solve the gas problem, but the trading module runs inconsistently and data delays have led to real losses.
apps.loved: The auto gas-fetch feature lets you work with tokens on new networks without buying the native token first.
apps.weak: Data in the trading module updates with a delay, which is critical during active trading.
apps.whoFor: DeFi users who need a non-custodial wallet with multi-network support.

apps.title: CoinMarketCap: Crypto Tracker
apps.verdict: CoinMarketCap is the de facto standard for tracking the crypto market: data on thousands of coins, exchange volumes, historical charts, and a portfolio tracker all work reliably. Recent updates added intrusive ads on launch and an aggressive Alpha section replacing familiar news, noticeably degrading the daily experience.
apps.loved: Market data is exhaustive: finding any coin with volume and history takes seconds.
apps.weak: Launch ads and replacing the news section with an opaque Alpha section irritate regular users.
apps.whoFor: A crypto investor who needs one source for market data.

quotes.text: The latest forced update now has pop-up ads on app start, and ads all over the place. Nobody wants ads thrown at them, we get enough of those everywhere else.
The ads they've added recently when I just want to check the BTC price has made it unusable for me. Deleted

apps.title: Kraken Pro: Advanced Trading
apps.verdict: A professional trading tool with a good interface and limit orders, but with noticeable chart lag relative to order book data, which is critical for precise entry. Support has been fully handed over to AI with no access to a live agent.
apps.loved: Advanced order types, trailing stop, and a customizable interface are valued by active traders.
apps.weak: The chart lags behind order book data, causing stop-losses and entry points to trigger incorrectly.
apps.whoFor: An experienced active trader who needs a professional terminal on a smartphone.

quotes.text: App works. If you need customer support, you will be in a world of pain. Everything is AI based and you will not be able to talk to a real person. Good luck in this nightmare. UPDATE: Kraken made it right within 48 hours. Still never spoke to a real person, but my issue was resolved in a timely man

App is ok for trading after using 3 different exchange apps. They all got their pros and cons. Two stars for support answers bring copy and pasting their website links. Can't answer questions or solve problems.

apps.title: Uniswap: Crypto & NFT Wallet
apps.verdict: Best-in-class non-custodial wallet for Web3 with reliable DEX swapping and good multi-network support. The main problem right now: the mobile app has degraded in speed, with launch times growing to 3 to 5 minutes, which is critical for trading.
apps.loved: Non-custodial swap directly in the wallet without registration or verification.
apps.weak: The app takes several minutes to launch and is unstable on iOS, while the browser extension works fine.
apps.whoFor: DeFi users working with tokens not available on major exchanges.

quotes.text: It'd be great if we could see the Return % and Unrealized Return. Thanks

apps.title: CryptoPanic
apps.verdict: CryptoPanic handles the job of quickly catching up with the crypto market news backdrop: it aggregates sources in one place and helps explain the why behind price moves. The downside is that the app has not been updated in years, notifications arrive an hour late, and the mobile UI suffers from small font.
apps.loved: Pulls news from specialized crypto publications into a single feed, saving time on monitoring.
apps.weak: Notifications about important events arrive an hour or more late, making them useless for decision-making.
apps.whoFor: Investors who need a quick news context without switching between websites.

apps.title: Gate: Trade BTC & ETH
apps.verdict: Gate.io offers one of the widest asset catalogs among centralized exchanges, including US stocks, and is highly regarded by active traders. The main problem: account lockout when changing a phone number, verification stops working, and funds are effectively frozen permanently.
apps.loved: Huge selection of coins, crypto and US stocks in one app, highly rated by experienced traders.
apps.weak: Losing access to the linked phone number means an irreversible account lockout with funds inside.
apps.whoFor: Experienced traders who need a wide market and futures tools.

apps.title: Public: Invest & Trade
apps.verdict: Public stands out for support quality and a clean interface for long-term investing. The main product limitation: the options toolset has been incomplete for years, and data does not go below the one-minute timeframe.
apps.loved: Live and fast support that users praise as the best in the category.
apps.weak: Options trading works inconsistently: rolling and selling options break with every major update.
apps.whoFor: A passive stock and ETF investor who values service.

quotes.text: Overall the app is pretty decent, better than most I used , but one thing keeping me from staying with this brokerage is that , they Charge fees on Recurring investments, fidelity robinhood, or many others do not charge recurring investments which is the way most people should invest, set it recurri

apps.title: STRIKE: Buy & Hold Bitcoin
apps.verdict: A specialized Bitcoin service with Lightning support and direct paycheck-to-bitcoin debiting, which sets it apart from general exchanges. Weekly deposit limits and the inability to scan Lightning QR codes slow down more active users.
apps.loved: Direct paycheck-to-bitcoin routing and Lightning transfers in one app.
apps.weak: Lightning QR codes do not work and users have to copy invoices manually, which is awkward for everyday payments.
apps.whoFor: A bitcoin maximalist building an accumulation strategy through regular deposits.

quotes.text: Love the app, just wish there was a way to actually track how much I'm up on my investment. Only way to kind of see is to go through all my deposits and add them up, then see what my current position value is at.
Can't have recurring buys of same frequency, as in can't have 2 weekly recurring buys

apps.title: Edge - Crypto & Bitcoin Wallet
apps.verdict: A non-custodial privacy-focused wallet supporting a wide range of networks and coins, but slow transactions and rare cases of balance disappearing during resync seriously undermine trust.
apps.loved: Support for many networks, built-in exchange, and a privacy focus with Nym mixnet integration.
apps.weak: After a resync command the wallet sometimes shows a zero balance for up to several days, causing panic among users.
apps.whoFor: Advanced users for whom privacy and self-custody matter.

apps.title: Coinbase: Buy Crypto & Stocks
apps.verdict: Coinbase is the most accessible way for a beginner to enter crypto: verification works, trading is clear, and liquidity is there. The main weakness is holds on funds that appear unexpectedly, and support can take months to resolve an issue.
apps.loved: After verification, buying and selling bitcoin is easier here than anywhere else.
apps.weak: Temporary holds on funds arrive with no clear explanation and can last for weeks.
apps.whoFor: A beginner buying bitcoin or ether for the first time.

quotes.text: Coinbase advertised instant funding/trading availability for prediction markets, but after depositing $10,000 via bank transfer, my funds were marked as unavailable with almost no clear explanation in the UI. The app showed the balance in my account but only $0.01 available to trade. The distinction

I hate how coinbase has switched its focus to gambling on anything and everything. It's one thing if it was just a section I don't have to go to on the app, but the constant notifications are starting to piss me off. They will send you so many notifications on games that are starting and you can gam

Do not trust Coinbase with the majority of your money It's really great until you have a problem.... it's great to buy and sell, but keep most of your money in a D centralized wallet!! When I have an issue with Coinbase the customer service representatives are very nice! But nothing actually gets fi

apps.title: Exodus: Crypto & Payments
apps.verdict: A beautiful and relatively accessible non-custodial wallet, but ETH staking hangs in an undefined state for extended periods, and navigating transaction history is not intuitive. Suitable for beginners with caveats.
apps.loved: A unique visual interface and wide coin support attract those who want to keep everything in one place.
apps.weak: ETH staking enters limbo for months with no clear status or timeline.
apps.whoFor: A crypto beginner looking for a beautiful and relatively simple wallet.

quotes.text: Why I rated it 4 instead of 5 was because I just started using it so i haven't fully gone into it yet but from what I'm seeing I'm loving the app very much, as a beginner it's easier to scale through it & understand things & I hope on the long run it doesn't disappoint me

I staked ETH 2 months ago and the wallet says the staking is STILL in process. I can't even attempt to unstake it because it is in literal limbo. There's no way it takes 60 days for the staking to be complete. There's help section has a lot of words but doesn't give a range of expected staking time.

apps.title: CoinTracking
apps.verdict: CoinTracking fills the niche of tax accounting and crypto portfolio tracking at a level most competitors cannot match. The mobile app is significantly weaker than the web version: transactions cannot be added manually, charts periodically stop working, and the interface is dated.
apps.loved: Automatic import from exchanges and tax-basis calculation under different accounting methods saves hours at year end.
apps.weak: You cannot add a trade manually from the mobile app, so the core feature is unavailable on the go.
apps.whoFor: Serious investors with portfolios across multiple exchanges who need tax accounting.

apps.title: Zerion: Crypto Wallet & DeFi
apps.verdict: Zerion handles multi-chain portfolio aggregation well and can find hidden assets like Aave rewards that are unavailable in other wallets. Regularly breaking Ledger connectivity after updates is a serious issue for hardware wallet users.
apps.loved: A single dashboard for tracking assets across dozens of networks with accurate DeFi position display.
apps.weak: Ledger hardware wallet integration is unstable and breaks after app updates.
apps.whoFor: Advanced DeFi users with assets across multiple networks.

apps.title: TabTrader - crypto terminal
apps.verdict: TabTrader works as a multi-exchange terminal with solid charts and alerts, but aggressively moving basic features behind a paywall and the gap between iOS and Android versions disappoint loyal users.
apps.loved: A unified terminal for multiple exchanges with customizable alerts saves time for experienced traders.
apps.weak: iOS lacks API-based trading even though the Android version has had it for years.
apps.whoFor: Traders working across multiple exchanges simultaneously.

apps.title: Webull: Investing & Trading
apps.verdict: Webull is built for serious traders: attractive charts, futures, advanced orders, and Turbo Trader genuinely set it apart among mobile brokers. The problem is periodic account restrictions without explanation and order execution bugs that are dangerous for active trading.
apps.loved: Charts and technical analysis tools on mobile are the best in their segment.
apps.weak: Accounts go into restriction without warning and support does not respond for weeks.
apps.whoFor: An active trader who needs futures and professional charts on a phone.

apps.title: Crypto Pro: Live Coin Tracker
apps.verdict: Crypto Pro offers a clean tracker with a friendly interface, metals support, and widgets. However, several key features have been broken for years without a fix: favorites are lost, widgets reset, and developers do not respond to user reports.
apps.loved: A clean and fast tracker interface with metals support and a customizable watchlist.
apps.weak: The portfolio periodically wipes completely and restoring from an iCloud backup does not recover the data.
apps.whoFor: A passive crypto holder watching prices without active trading.

quotes.text: Used to be great but was seemingly abandoned by the developers. No update in 8 months and the widgets haven't worked in almost as long

apps.title: Crypto Tracker by BitScreener
apps.verdict: A reliable tracker with solid price alerts and a handy portfolio that users have relied on for years. The main problem is not the data but infrastructure degradation: alerts stop working, deleted notifications keep firing, and support does not respond for months.
apps.loved: Price alerts work near real-time and have become a reliable tool for traders.
apps.weak: Deleted alerts keep firing and it is impossible to fix this through support.
apps.whoFor: Traders who need fast price monitoring without a built-in exchange.

apps.title: Delta by eToro
apps.verdict: Delta by eToro remains one of the best portfolio aggregators for those who hold both crypto and stocks in one place. The main weakness since the eToro transition: performance has dropped and support for many brokers has not materialized.
apps.loved: A single screen for crypto and equity portfolios with a pleasant visualization of performance.
apps.weak: Sync with popular brokers like Schwab and Merrill Lynch is advertised but has not worked for years.
apps.whoFor: Individual investors combining crypto and the stock market.

quotes.text: Used to be better when it was completely free. I understand why they add a fee, wish it was less but glad they keep making improvements to the app.

apps.title: Changelly Exchange・Buy Crypto
apps.verdict: Changelly works as an aggregator for quick swaps between wallets, shows the network fee upfront, and does not hold assets. Weaknesses include high slippage through partners like Moonpay, no transaction history inside the app, and occasional execution delays.
apps.loved: Network fee breakdown is shown before confirming the swap, with no hidden markup at checkout.
apps.weak: Transaction history is not accessible inside the app even though money flows through it.
apps.whoFor: Users who need to quickly transfer assets between wallets without registering on an exchange.

apps.title: Rain: Buy & Sell Bitcoin
apps.verdict: The only exchange with instant bank deposit and withdrawal in the UAE around the clock, making it indispensable for local expats, but verification periodically blocks accounts without a clear explanation.
apps.loved: Instant bank transfers 24 hours a day in the UAE with no delays, unavailable on other platforms.
apps.weak: The new interface removed the ability to sort coins and filter the list by active positions.
apps.whoFor: Expats and residents of the UAE and Bahrain who actively trade crypto.

apps.title: RedotPay: Crypto Card & Pay
apps.verdict: A globally covered crypto card with fast transactions and Apple Pay, but after several updates the app stops opening and customer support is slow to respond.
apps.loved: The card works worldwide through Apple Pay and lets you pay with crypto where it is not accepted directly.
apps.weak: A lifetime limit of five cards per account that does not reset even after deleting old cards.
apps.whoFor: Those living in countries with limited access to payment infrastructure.

apps.title: Crypto Master: Market Analysis
apps.verdict: A set of crypto market analysis tools with real data and screeners, but the search bar systematically breaks after updates and ads cannot be turned off in the paid version.
apps.loved: An extensive set of technical indicators and screeners with real-time quotes all in one place.
apps.weak: After several updates, searching coins by symbol stopped working and searching by name returns an empty chart.
apps.whoFor: Technical analysts who follow the market from their phone.

apps.title: Bybit: Buy Crypto & Bitcoin
apps.verdict: Bybit offers a broad trading toolkit for experienced traders with a solid derivatives lineup. The unresolved core product issue: two-factor authentication via Google Authenticator works with hour-long delays, and a recent navigation overhaul removed the persistent bottom bar.
apps.loved: A rich set of trading instruments including futures and options on a single platform.
apps.weak: Two-factor authentication via Google Authenticator accepts codes with up to an hour delay, blocking access at the worst moment.
apps.whoFor: An experienced derivatives trader outside the US.

apps.title: eToro: Investing made social
apps.verdict: eToro works as a social investing platform with copy trading and wide asset coverage, but withdrawals remain a painful process and the app is unstable during peak trading hours.
apps.loved: The social layer and copying trades from popular investors lowers the barrier to entry for beginners.
apps.weak: Token delistings happen without in-app notifications, leaving users with positions they had no chance to exit.
apps.whoFor: Beginner investors who want to follow experienced traders.

apps.title: BitPay: Buy Bitcoin & Ethereum
apps.verdict: A non-custodial wallet with multisig and broad coin support, but the purchase UX is confusing: you need to hold gas in the right network, and email support is slow.
apps.loved: A multi-currency non-custodial wallet with multisig support and easy gift card purchases.
apps.weak: To send a token you must separately hold gas for the right network, which is never explained to newcomers.
apps.whoFor: Those who want to hold crypto independently without relying on an exchange.

apps.title: Bitcoin.com Wallet: Buy, sell
apps.verdict: Bitcoin.com Wallet works reliably as a non-custodial wallet for basic bitcoin storage and sending. The key product flaw is not the fee size itself but the opacity: the stated percentage differs from the final amount, and manual control over the network fee has been removed.
apps.loved: Non-custodial storage with a simple interface suits those holding bitcoin for the first time.
apps.weak: Manual network fee selection has been removed, taking away control over transactions from experienced users.
apps.whoFor: A newcomer who wants to buy and hold bitcoin once.

apps.title: Crypto.com: Buy BTC, ETH & CRO
apps.verdict: Crypto.com offers a wide range of coins, staking, and a beginner-friendly interface, but navigation to deposit and withdrawal is deliberately confusing, support is chatbot-only, and wallet lockouts lasting weeks leave users without access to their assets.
apps.loved: Coin variety and a simple purchase screen work well for those just getting started.
apps.weak: Withdrawals and account management are buried several menu levels deep and the interface offers no forgiveness for mistakes.
apps.whoFor: A newcomer who wants to buy coins beyond bitcoin and ether.

quotes.text: They don't even have a proper support team. Just some Ai chatbots to handle anything. Including hacks or scams

I just get frustrated because I really don't know what I'm doing here. I bought Cro & XRP , but don't understand what to do. I've been staking my Cro but I don't even know or understand what I'm doing.

apps.title: MetaMask: Trade Crypto
apps.verdict: MetaMask remains the most widely used Web3 wallet with broad network and dApp support. The core product issue is not price but instability: after updates, network settings disappear, the interface lags, and scanning a QR code to send is hidden in a non-obvious menu.
apps.loved: Access to a vast dApp ecosystem and multi-network support in one wallet.
apps.weak: The interface degrades after updates: network settings disappear, buttons get covered by the keyboard, and the hardware wallet via Bluetooth is unreliable.
apps.whoFor: A DeFi and Web3 user with blockchain experience.

apps.title: CoinTracker: Portfolio & Taxes
apps.verdict: The only mainstream tool for tracking a crypto portfolio with a focus on tax reporting that actually works when set up correctly. The weak point: the mobile app syncs data slower than the web version and prices lag.
apps.loved: Automatically aggregates transactions from dozens of wallets and exchanges for a tax return.
apps.weak: Portfolio balance in the app updates with a delay and may show incorrect profit/loss colors.
apps.whoFor: Active traders working across multiple exchanges and preparing tax filings.

apps.title: Arzdigital
apps.verdict: Arzdigital works as a crypto data aggregator for a Persian-speaking audience and handles its job in calm periods, but regular updates break the app: crashes after a release have become an expected pattern, not an exception.
apps.loved: A convenient watchlist and a Persian-language news feed address a real need for an audience without access to global platforms.
apps.weak: Every major update is followed by widespread crashes and users have to wait weeks for a patch.
apps.whoFor: Persian-speaking investors following the crypto market.

apps.title: Tonkeeper: Crypto & TON Wallet
apps.verdict: A TON ecosystem wallet with a clean interface, but it crashes regularly on specific devices and shows spam tokens on the balance that cannot be hidden. Removing the swap section has significantly cut the product's value.
apps.loved: Simple UX, fast navigation, and the Battery feature that covers the network fee on your behalf.
apps.weak: Spam tokens appear in the balance and cannot be hidden, and the swap section was removed without a clear replacement.
apps.whoFor: Users of TON and Telegram mini-apps.

apps.title: The Crypto App: News & Alerts
apps.verdict: The app offers a convenient portfolio tracker and flexible price alerts, but the iOS version is unstable: widgets break after updates, favorite coins reset, and crashes on launch are reported by many users.
apps.loved: An informative interface with a wide coin selection and functional home-screen widgets when they work.
apps.weak: Favorite coins reset on their own and widgets stop updating after an update with no way to fix it short of reinstalling.
apps.whoFor: Investors who need a tracker without trading.

apps.title: SoFi: Bank, Invest & Crypto
apps.verdict: SoFi tries to be a bank, broker, and crypto wallet all at once, but reliably handles none of those roles: promo bonuses are not paid out, IPO allocations are opaque, and the support chat crashes when you try to use it. The idea of combining everything in one place is appealing, but execution is rough enough to outweigh the convenience.
apps.loved: The ability to keep savings, stocks, and crypto in a single app is genuinely convenient.
apps.weak: The investment section does not show accumulated P&L and lacks the tools needed to manage positions.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants one account instead of three separate apps.

apps.title: Uphold: Buy BTC, ETH and 360+
apps.verdict: Uphold wins on breadth of assets and staking unavailable at major competitors. However, the security system is too aggressive: accounts get blocked without warning for weeks and support goes silent.
apps.loved: Wide crypto asset selection and built-in staking in one place attract those who care about variety.
apps.weak: The account-blocking algorithm triggers arbitrarily and leaves users without access to their funds for months with no explanation.
apps.whoFor: Crypto holders with non-standard assets who are willing to accept unpredictable support.

quotes.text: The application will hold your money with no basis or reasoning. They will not respond for 6 months timeframe. I lost all my liquidity because of this. Beware! I know an entire community of people who experienced the same thing.

I was hopeful that I would make something out of the investment I made. However that was not the case here. It only took a day for my initial investment to drop! It continued to drop and being a new investor with little to no help, I had no idea what to invest in to being making a profit.

For an old dog like me the app download and set up was a little difficult for me. But, I was able to get it all set up. Uphold has "staking" which I understand other platforms don't do. I also have more crypto choices than other popular platforms. I'm so happy I accidentally picked uphold!

Went to withdraw some much-needed money like I have many times before and what am I hit with when opening the app? A DEMAND for selfie verification. I've used this app for years. FaceID allowed. 2FA setup. Why do I need to provide a selfie now?! And I can't proceed until I do?!

apps.title: HODL Real-Time Crypto Tracker
apps.verdict: Once the best crypto price aggregator, it has degraded: real-time data freezes regularly, notifications arrive 10 or more hours late, ads overlap charts, and support returns a 404. The core product is broken.
apps.loved: The simplicity and clarity of the portfolio tracker have not been surpassed by competitors in terms of usability.
apps.weak: Prices stop updating in real time and price notifications arrive hours late, making them meaningless.
apps.whoFor: A passive holder who needs rough tracking without precise timing.

quotes.text: If you love nonstop Temu ads that prevent you from seeing charts, this is the app for you!

This was a great app with a very good free tier. They added ads which were not bad at all. The newest change though is what ruined it. You are now limited to tracking and displaying only 10 coins or stocks at one time.

apps.title: CEX.IO: Crypto Wallet/Exchange
apps.verdict: CEX.IO operates as an exchange with a long history, but users regularly get stuck during verification or withdrawal without an explanation. Support is overloaded and responds slowly.
apps.loved: The platform runs stably for basic purchases and storage for those who passed verification without issues.
apps.weak: The withdrawal process is opaque: errors appear without cause and users spend weeks trying to get their money out.
apps.whoFor: Experienced users who have already passed KYC and do not plan frequent withdrawals.

quotes.text: This app is not advise able to use at all, since the first day I've purchased bitcoin on this app after verification of my account I was unable to withdraw my fund to my other wallet even to the account user it just keep telling me that kyc I don't understand the hell the app is all about

apps.title: Robinhood Wallet: Swap Crypto
apps.verdict: Robinhood Wallet works as a basic non-custodial wallet on Ethereum, but after dropping Polygon it lost its main advantage of cheap swaps. Spam token filtering is weak, Bitcoin is not supported, and integration with the main Robinhood app is minimal.
apps.loved: A familiar brand and simple interface lower the barrier to non-custodial storage.
apps.weak: Dropping Polygon support eliminated affordable swaps and left only expensive Ethereum.
apps.whoFor: Robinhood users taking their first steps in self-custody crypto.

apps.title: Cash App
apps.verdict: Cash App positions itself as a simple tool for money transfers and basic bitcoin storage, but the core problem is mass unexplained account blocks and situations where sent money never reaches the recipient. For a financial tool, reliability is everything, and that is precisely where it falls seriously short.
apps.loved: When everything works, transfers go through instantly and conveniently.
apps.weak: Accounts are blocked without warning or explanation and appeals are automatically rejected.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants to quickly send a small amount to a friend.

quotes.text: Cash App seems to be deactivating random accounts without reason nor will they give a reason. I opened my app today to realize my account was deactivated without warning or a reason. I called support and the representative said they could not tell me why and asked if I would like to appeal. I agreed

Cash App used to be a simple way to send and receive money. Now it feels like a nonstop advertising platform that occasionally handles payments. The app is constantly pushing promotions, offers, and features I have no interest in using.

apps.title: Phantom - Trade Markets
apps.verdict: Phantom won the market as the main Solana wallet, but aggressive interface overhauls after each update break familiar flows, and reports of coins disappearing during price spikes undermine trust in reliability. The product runs inconsistently for memecoin trading.
apps.loved: Transaction confirmation speed on Solana and the clean base interface design.
apps.weak: Coins disappear from the portfolio during price spikes and reappear after the move, making active trading unreliable.
apps.whoFor: A long-term Solana asset holder who is not actively trading.

apps.title: SafePal: Crypto Wallet BTC NFT
apps.verdict: A multi-network wallet with broad blockchain support and the SafePal S1 hardware wallet, but the portfolio updates incorrectly, transaction notifications do not work, and after app updates users lose access to tokens despite a saved seed phrase.
apps.loved: Supports more networks and coins than most competitors, including pairing with the hardware wallet.
apps.weak: Portfolio balances show nonexistent tokens and fail to sync correctly after updates.
apps.whoFor: Experienced holders of a large variety of coins across multiple networks.

apps.title: LOBSTR Wallet: Buy XLM & XRP
apps.verdict: LOBSTR remains a working wallet for XLM if all you need is to hold and send Stellar assets. Everything beyond that scenario, swapping, withdrawing through MoonPay, working with other tokens, is difficult and often ends in lost funds.
apps.loved: For an XLM wallet the interface is clean and clear, and Stellar blockchain transaction speed is high.
apps.whoFor: XLM holders who do not plan to swap assets.

apps.title: MEXC: Buy Bitcoin & Crypto
apps.verdict: MEXC draws traders with a wide coin selection and no spot fees, but its risk-control system blocks withdrawals precisely for successful traders, turning an advantage into a trap. Regulatory issues and forced KYC make the platform unpredictable.
apps.loved: A massive selection of altcoins and high leverage attract traders who need access to low-liquidity coins.
apps.weak: The risk-control mechanism triggers arbitrarily and blocks withdrawals with no avenue for appeal.
apps.whoFor: Speculative traders willing to accept unpredictability in exchange for access to rare tokens.

apps.title: Luno: Buy Crypto and US Stocks
apps.verdict: The platform onboards newcomers in Africa well with a clear interface, but systematically blocks withdrawals and leaves people locked out of accounts for years, which destroys trust in the product.
apps.loved: Easy signup and a clear interface for those buying crypto for the first time.
apps.weak: Verification is not required for deposits but the system freezes and fails to complete checks for months when you withdraw.
apps.whoFor: Beginner investors in Nigeria and South Africa.

apps.title: Binance.US: Buy BTC & Crypto
apps.verdict: Binance.US is a stripped-down US version of global Binance, and you can feel it: transaction history is available for only 90 days, P&L must be calculated manually, the interface is confusing, and support can deactivate accounts without explanation. Low fees and reliable order execution are real advantages, but the product is technically rough.
apps.loved: Fees are among the lowest of any regulated US exchange.
apps.weak: Trading history is cut to 90 days and there is no automatic profit and loss calculation.
apps.whoFor: A trader who wants low fees and is willing to accept limited functionality.

apps.title: Plus500 Trading & Investing
apps.verdict: Plus500 offers a wide range of CFD instruments with fast withdrawals, but the mobile app slows down precisely during volatility, when it matters most, and execution failures during position closing turn profit into loss.
apps.loved: Regular traders note same-day withdrawals without bureaucracy.
apps.weak: Charts and quotes lag during high volatility, making precise entry and exit from a position unreliable.
apps.whoFor: CFD traders with small positions who do not depend on tick-level accuracy.

apps.title: MEW Wallet・Stocks and Crypto
apps.verdict: MEW can hold ether and tokens, but breaks regularly after updates with white screens. A forced migration from a 5-word phrase to a 24-word phrase cut off longtime users from their funds. Gamification and spam take up more space than stability.
apps.loved: A reputation as a secure wallet for Ethereum veterans and a beginner-friendly interface.
apps.weak: Migration to the new seed phrase format broke access for some users without warning.
apps.whoFor: ETH holders willing to tolerate periodic breakdowns.

apps.title: Webull Pay: Crypto Buy & Sell
apps.verdict: A separate Webull crypto app with the most fundamental structural flaw: you cannot withdraw crypto to an external wallet, only sell and withdraw fiat. This eliminates the point of any long-term self-custody crypto strategy.
apps.loved: Fast trades without extra information for those already comfortable in the Webull ecosystem.
apps.weak: Crypto assets cannot be transferred to your own wallet: only selling inside the app is possible.
apps.whoFor: Existing Webull clients who want to add crypto to their brokerage account without self-custody.

quotes.text: My recurring option it's not available

apps.title: Gemini Markets & Credit Card
apps.verdict: Gemini combines a crypto exchange and a crypto cashback credit card, which is an interesting combination, but the app consistently fails to deliver: the card blocks without notification, in-app payment stops working for months, charts fail to load, and staking orders execute in the opposite direction to what was entered. The product idea is more interesting than the product itself.
apps.loved: A credit card with bitcoin cashback is a rare and genuinely useful mechanic.
apps.weak: The credit card is regularly blocked for unclear reasons and restoring access through the app is impossible.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants to accumulate bitcoin through everyday card spending.

quotes.text: Closed my account and would not tell me why
Why am I getting sports notifications on my crypto app!? I can't even opt out of this BS. I just want crypto and completed order updates. I don't GAF about sports.
The photo id upload function is not working on this app! Also tech support is very slow

apps.title: GoMining: BTC Mining & Finance
apps.verdict: A cloud mining service that technically works, but profitability is wiped out by operating fees. Users who invested $400 in hashpower end up with less than if they had simply bought bitcoin for that amount.
apps.loved: A clear cloud mining mechanic with the ability to reinvest in hashpower directly from the app.
apps.weak: Maintenance and electricity fees consume most of the income, especially for small investments.
apps.whoFor: Those who want to participate in bitcoin mining without buying hardware and are prepared for a long payback period.

quotes.text: Met these folks at Consensus. Looked very interesting. Tried playing around with it but it was not clear to me what to do exactly. I did some of the academy modules. Interesting ish. Did a little research on them and decided not a scam. But reviews said it's not as easy or frictionless as it sounds.

Updated review: I've been playing this for over a year now. It's a money pit. ROI is effectively zero. The service fees pretty much wipe out anything you generate. If you have the money to invest in this game, don't bother: just go out and buy the crypto outright.

apps.title: Bitget- Trade bitcoin & crypto
apps.verdict: The exchange provides a broad trading toolkit, but verification often hits a dead end, points cannot be redeemed, and transferred funds periodically disappear from the balance. P2P also has scammers the platform does not filter out.
apps.loved: A user-friendly interface and wide selection of trading pairs for experienced traders.
apps.weak: Multi-step verification on every login and unpredictable balance behavior undermine trust in the platform.
apps.whoFor: Experienced traders in regions without access to top-tier exchanges.

apps.title: Toobit: Buy BTC, ETH & Crypto
apps.verdict: Toobit has the functionality of a full exchange with trading tools, but several independent users describe the same pattern: stop-losses do not trigger and positions are liquidated at the right moment, which is a sign of price manipulation.
apps.loved: The set of trading tools and automation suits experienced traders who cannot watch the chart constantly.
apps.weak: The advertised stop-loss mechanics and trading volume reward payouts do not work as described in the terms.
apps.whoFor: Traders looking for a smaller alternative exchange with a wide token list.

apps.title: BitMart: Buy Crypto & Stocks
apps.verdict: An exchange with a wide coin list including small altcoins, but users spend months unable to register because verification codes do not work, and some report being unable to withdraw funds for years.
apps.loved: A wide altcoin selection including coins unavailable on major exchanges.
apps.weak: Account creation stalls at the verification step: codes do not work and the problem has persisted for weeks.
apps.whoFor: Traders hunting low-liquidity altcoins at an early stage.

apps.title: Bitstamp by Robinhood: Buy BTC
apps.verdict: Bitstamp is an exchange with a long history, but mobile app operational execution has failed: transfers freeze for months, accounts are blocked without explanation, and support does not respond. The trading interface with its tools works, but access to funds does not.
apps.loved: Trading tools and charts are better than most competitors and experienced traders value the depth of functionality.
apps.weak: Support does not resolve frozen fund issues for weeks and months.
apps.whoFor: Experienced traders who care about charts and orders more than withdrawal speed.

apps.title: CozyWallet
apps.verdict: Among real reviews, a systemic problem emerges: users report locked funds, inability to send Tron or Ripple, stolen tokens, and complete silence from support. The claimed decentralization contradicts mandatory email registration.
apps.loved: Convenient Telegram integration and minimal swap fees inside the app.
apps.weak: Inability to withdraw certain coins and no support response when funds are locked.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone given current reviews.

apps.title: Trust: Crypto & Bitcoin Wallet
apps.verdict: Trust Wallet is designed as a non-custodial wallet with full key control, which sounds good in theory, but in practice the app crashes during swaps, the balance sometimes fails to display after receiving BTC, and reinstallation requires re-entering the seed phrase every few months. The safety of the app itself raises questions: several users report missing assets.
apps.loved: Support for a wide number of networks and tokens in one non-custodial wallet.
apps.weak: The app periodically stops working and requires reinstallation with seed phrase entry.
apps.whoFor: A user who needs a non-custodial wallet for multiple blockchains.

quotes.text: I'm trying to get back into crypto and for some reason I can't see my account or transactions history. Trying to get support but get some BOT! I can't get a real person!!??

apps.title: CoinCap
apps.verdict: CoinCap was once a convenient minimalist tracker, but the team stopped updating the app: the last update was several years ago, quotes lag, the watchlist does not scroll, and many coins are simply absent. It can no longer be used as a primary tracker.
apps.loved: When the app worked, it offered a clean portfolio chart as a single line over all time with no noise.
apps.weak: The coin list has not been updated in years and most current tokens are simply missing from the database.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state.

apps.title: ­Moonshot
apps.verdict: An app for memecoin trading with an opaque coin discovery mechanic: new tokens appear in the listing days after launch when all the upside is already gone. Price alerts do not work and accounts are blocked without explanation for a year or more.
apps.loved: A simple entry into the world of memecoins for those who have never bought crypto before.
apps.weak: Coins appear in the app days or weeks late, eliminating the point of early-stage trading.
apps.whoFor: A memecoin speculator willing to accept high risk and opaque terms.

apps.title: OKX: Buy Bitcoin BTC & Crypto
apps.verdict: The exchange core works, but the withdrawal mechanism is systemically broken: users cannot link a bank for withdrawal even though the same bank is accepted for deposits. A basic platform function is unavailable to a significant portion of the audience.
apps.loved: Trading operations and account top-ups go through without problems.
apps.weak: Withdrawals are blocked for most banks with no clear explanation.
apps.whoFor: Experienced traders who do not plan to withdraw money to a card.

quotes.text: Only put 5 so it will show… it's easy to add money no problem. But trying to withdraw is impossible. Let's you link a bank to add. But won't link a bank to withdraw. Don't use.. crypto.com way easy to use add and withdraw

I had a very frustrating experience with OKX. After using the platform and completing verification with the same documents I had previously provided, I was suddenly told that their system could not verify my identity. I contacted support multiple times over more than a week. Every representative gav

apps.title: sMiles: Bitcoin Rewards
apps.verdict: The app promises bitcoin for steps, but withdrawals of satoshis do not work for most users and some accounts have been drained without explanation. The product's value is destroyed at the reward redemption stage.
apps.loved: The idea of passively accumulating bitcoin by walking is appealing and keeps an audience engaged for years.
apps.weak: The step-counting mechanic stops arbitrarily mid-day with no explanation.
apps.whoFor: Bitcoin fans willing to tolerate instability for a passive income.

apps.title: Base: Built to Trade & Earn
apps.verdict: Base Wallet, formerly Coinbase Wallet, is going through a painful redesign: during the transition to the new version some users lost assets, EIP-7702 delegation blocks NFT transfers, Solana transactions fail, and support has not responded for months. The L2 wallet has potential but its current state is dangerous for real money.
apps.loved: Trading on the Base network runs fast and around the clock for those who had no migration issues.
apps.weak: App updates have repeatedly led to loss of access to assets with no recovery path.
apps.whoFor: A developer or experienced crypto user willing to take risks on a new L2 network.

apps.title: Sweat Wallet: Walk Into Crypto
apps.verdict: The move-to-earn concept is interesting, but core mechanics are broken: accumulated tokens get stuck in the jar, the balance calculates incorrectly, and the earned crypto asset effectively cannot be withdrawn. The product does not deliver on its main promise.
apps.loved: The idea of linking physical activity to a real reward genuinely motivates some users to walk more.
apps.weak: Tokens disappear into the jar and cannot be withdrawn even after the growth period ends.
apps.whoFor: A fitness enthusiast who values the motivation process itself more than actual income.

quotes.text: I placed my coins in Jars as encouraged and now I cannot get them out once growth is completed have tried multiple times.
This app has really motivated me to try to walk every single day. I feel happy every day!

I genuinely feel so scammed. I'm not sure why they even bother to promote cryptocurrency as an incentive when the app doesn't even work. I'm never able to pay out on my earned crypto it makes no sense. Please fix this bug.

Hey this is a great idea! Keeping people active to receive money! I just have one question, can you add the pling digital wallet to the list of card providers? I can't actually cash out any of the money rendering it useless.
Used to be great but too many steps to earn 1 SWEAT, fees are going thru the roof, slow to transact, prize draws cost more and seems like chance of winning gets slimmer.

apps.title: Crypto.com: Onchain Wallet
apps.verdict: The wallet is positioned as non-custodial, but users are widely reporting frozen funds and unauthorized transfers after using the DApp browser. Losing access to an account with no support response turns asset storage into a lottery.
apps.loved: The interface is simple and clear for a newcomer, and trading fees on Cronos EVM are low.
apps.weak: After interacting with DApps, funds disappear and customer support does not respond.
apps.whoFor: Those who want to try Web3 with a minimal amount and accept the risks.

apps.title: MoonPay: Buy Crypto
apps.verdict: MoonPay exists as a payment gateway for buying crypto but is unreliable: money is charged and crypto does not reach the wallet, conversions lose funds without a trace in history, and support is automated and useless.
apps.loved: When a transaction goes through correctly, the crediting speed is faster than a bank transfer.
apps.weak: Purchased assets regularly do not arrive in the user's wallet and support cannot trace the transaction.
apps.whoFor: Users of embedded MoonPay payments in another service with no choice.

apps.title: Coinme: Buy Bitcoin & Crypto
apps.verdict: Coinme offers a unique niche: buying crypto with cash at a supermarket through a Coinstar terminal. But execution is unreliable: coins do not get credited, accounts are blocked right after registration, and customer service runs only through a bot. The concept is interesting but the product is rough.
apps.loved: The ability to buy crypto with cash at an ordinary supermarket without a bank card is a unique scenario for the unbanked.
apps.weak: Purchased coins regularly do not get credited to the account and support cannot fix it.
apps.whoFor: Those who want to buy crypto with cash and have no access to online exchanges.

apps.title: BTCC - Trade Bitcoin & Crypto
apps.verdict: BTCC draws newcomers with generous bonuses that turn out to be useless coupons, and several users point out this discrepancy directly. User funds periodically disappear, copy trading eats profits with fees, and the app closes on its own.
apps.loved: Educational materials and a demo mode help newcomers understand the basics of crypto trading.
apps.weak: Advertised bonuses are trading coupons with no real value, which erodes trust in the platform.
apps.whoFor: No one who plans to invest real money.

apps.title: Best: Bitcoin & Crypto Wallet
apps.verdict: Best Wallet is positioned as a Web3 wallet with presales, but systemic complaints about being unable to withdraw assets and losing access to funds make it an unreliable tool for holding real value.
apps.loved: Access to presale tokens unavailable on regular exchanges attracts an early investor audience.
apps.weak: Some users have been unable to withdraw assets for months, destroying the core property of any wallet which is control over your own funds.
apps.whoFor: Crypto presale participants willing to accept elevated risk.

apps.title: KCEX: The Lowest Crypto Fees
apps.verdict: Several independent users from different countries describe the same pattern: verification passed, coins purchased, then the account is blocked without explanation and funds are not returned. Low fees do not compensate for the high risk of losing funds.
apps.loved: A clean interface, genuinely low trading fees, and a wide range of coins on spot and futures.
apps.weak: Withdrawals are blocked for vague risk-control reasons with no appeal and waits of up to 30 days.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state.

apps.title: Finelo: Master Trading
apps.verdict: The app is positioned as trading education, but the real content boils down to common knowledge you can find on Wikipedia. The core problem is not money but that the product as such does not exist: after registration users cannot log into their account.
apps.loved: A visually appealing onboarding gives a sense of an easy start in the first few minutes.
apps.weak: The educational content is shallow enough that the app offers nothing not found in any free article.

apps.title: XRP Wallet: Trade & Buy Crypto
apps.verdict: The wallet fails at the basic job: users widely report being unable to withdraw XRP, blocked funds, and a compromised cold wallet. The app is not authorized by Ripple yet positions itself as an XRP wallet, which is a warning sign in itself.
apps.loved: Customer support sometimes helps recover account access by email.
apps.weak: Withdrawals and transfers work unreliably or not at all.
apps.whoFor: Cautious experimenters with a zero balance.

apps.title: Metal Pay: Buy Bitcoin and ETH
apps.verdict: Metal Pay fails the basic reliability test: the app does not open for a significant portion of users, account verification freezes, and support is unreachable. The core function of a crypto payment platform is inaccessible to many.
apps.loved: The XPR token attracts its own audience as a niche asset unavailable on major exchanges.
apps.weak: The app freezes on the loading screen and will not let users through, making all other functionality unreachable.
apps.whoFor: XPR token holders who have no alternative.

apps.title: Paybis Wallet: Buy Bitcoin
apps.verdict: A crypto purchase service with systemic verification problems: money is charged before the check is completed, transactions are then declined, and refunds drag on for days with no coherent support.
apps.loved: In the rare cases where transactions work, the process is fast and requires no extra steps.
apps.weak: The system charges the card before verifying identity and then blocks the transaction after charging, without immediately returning the funds.

apps.title: Bitcoin Mining: Crypto Miner
apps.verdict: The app mines very slowly but withdrawal thresholds are set so high that cashing out is practically impossible. Users with real calculations show that a $300 yearly subscription yields $14 to $33 in returns.
apps.loved: The accumulation mechanic through watching ads runs stably and requires no investment to start.
apps.weak: Hashrate earned by watching ads is systematically reduced over time and the withdrawal threshold makes earnings practically out of reach.
apps.whoFor: Those who want to understand how mining works without real investment.

quotes.text: Don't bother downloading. It will take you 5 years to mine $20 worth of BTC and have to suffer through 5000 ad videos

… I spent $300 for 5 annual plans (60% off sale). I have watchedd videos, regularly acquired the free 8 hour contract, and the daily loyalty bonus multiplier. I am 14 days in and I have earned $0.57. That pace results in $14.86 after the 1 year term. Be aware of buying contracts!

apps.title: BRD Bitcoin Wallet
apps.verdict: BRD has effectively ceased to exist as an independent product: new users cannot use it and existing users must migrate to Coinbase Wallet. There is no point in downloading it.
apps.loved: In the past it stood out for simplicity and clear private key management without unnecessary complexity.
apps.weak: The app is non-functional for new users and leads only to a migration page.
apps.whoFor: No one except those restoring an old wallet.

apps.title: Anchor - Buy Bitcoin and Ether
apps.verdict: Anchor has accumulated a critical mass of complaints about blocked withdrawals and a failed banking partner for months: users cannot deposit or withdraw. Limit orders do not execute on time and support responds with automated messages.
apps.loved: A debit card and simple interface are liked by a small number of long-term users.
apps.weak: The banking integration has been broken for many months, blocking both deposits and withdrawals.
apps.whoFor: No one at the current stage of platform operation.

apps.title: Gocrypto: Crypto Trading
apps.verdict: Reviews give no way to establish what this product is: users ask basic questions about whether they can withdraw money at all, and several report vanished portfolios and account takeovers. No real value proposition can be traced.
apps.loved: Newcomers like that the interface is not overloaded with information.
apps.weak: The withdrawal mechanic is opaque or inaccessible to most users.
apps.whoFor: Impossible to determine at the current level of transparency.

apps.title: Cryptoguru: Trading Academy
apps.verdict: No real educational product is visible in the reviews at all. Substantive reviews are almost nonexistent, and the few that make sense describe intrusive ads and the inability to withdraw simulated funds.
apps.loved: The app looks like a trading simulator without real risk.
apps.weak: Simulated earnings cannot be withdrawn and ads block the interface.
apps.whoFor: Curious newcomers who want a gamified trading simulation.

apps.title: Bitcoin Mining · Cloud Mining
apps.verdict: The app offers pseudo-mining through ads: the balance grows and then resets without explanation, and withdrawal is blocked until an unreachable threshold is met. The mechanic keeps users around for ad impressions, not real income.
apps.loved: A few users report a successful withdrawal via Lightning Network in a couple of seconds.
apps.weak: The accumulated balance resets or freezes arbitrarily, making any long-term participation pointless.
apps.whoFor: The curious who are willing to watch ads without expecting real earnings.

quotes.text: I invested in this for almost 2 years thinking it would keep running only to find out the mining STALLED. Now it wants me to watch ads just to keep it going. Total scam. Do NOT spend a dime you'll lose your money just like I did. Also I I had about $27 in bitcoin To find out I can withdraw nothi
